info.text: Unit 13 — Querying a Service Bulletin with the OEM. Listening · Reading · Use of English · Vocabulary.

name.text: U13-L1 Dialogue 1 — is the aircraft affected?

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. The technician gives serial number 5127. Is the aircraft affected by the bulletin?

generalfeedback.text: The OEM says: "Serial 5127 is inside the effectivity. Your aircraft is affected." Being inside the effectivity is exactly what "affected" means.

answer.text: Yes, it is inside the effectivity.

feedback.text: Correct — the serial is inside the effectivity, so the aircraft is affected.

answer.text: No, it is outside the effectivity.

feedback.text: No — the OEM confirms 5127 is inside the effectivity.
No — the answer does not depend on a future revision.

answer.text: The OEM could not confirm it.

feedback.text: No — the OEM confirms it clearly on the call.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. True or false: the bulletin is mandatory.

generalfeedback.text: False. The OEM says it is "recommended, not mandatory" and is "not linked to an airworthiness directive". Only an AD would make it mandatory.

feedback.text: Correct — it is recommended; no AD is linked.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. Write the aircraft serial number the technician reads out (digits only).

generalfeedback.text: The technician says "five-one-two-seven" — serial 5127.

name.text: U13-L4 Dialogue 2 — what makes it mandatory?

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. What makes the modification mandatory for the affected aircraft?

generalfeedback.text: An airworthiness directive (AD) makes the modification mandatory. A service bulletin on its own is only recommended unless an AD is linked to it.

feedback.text: No — a revision number does not set the compliance level.
No — lead time is about parts supply, not compliance.
No — compliance level is not the engineer's choice.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. Compliance is due within how many months of the airworthiness directive date? (number only)

generalfeedback.text: The OEM says compliance is due "within twelve months of the airworthiness directive date" — 12 months.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. True or false: revision 3 is the current revision.

generalfeedback.text: True. The OEM says "Revision three is current. Revision two is superseded, so please do not use it."

feedback.text: Correct — revision 3 is current; revision 2 is superseded.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. The lead time for the modification kit is about how many weeks? (number only)

generalfeedback.text: The OEM says the lead time is "about three weeks" and advises ordering the kit soon.

questiontext.text: Listen to the OEM voicemail again. Which revision is now current?

generalfeedback.text: The voicemail says revision 2 is now superseded and revision 3 is current from today; two more serials are now affected, but the modification stays recommended.

feedback.text: No — revision 3 is clearly named as current.

questiontext.text:
Read this service bulletin excerpt.

SERVICE BULLETIN 32-1150, REV 1. Subject: main landing gear door seal — replacement. Compliance: recommended. This bulletin is not linked to an airworthiness directive. The manufacturer advises action at the next scheduled check.

According to the excerpt, compliance is:

generalfeedback.text: The text states "Compliance: recommended" and that no AD is linked, so the action is advised but not required by law.

feedback.text: No — no deadline or AD is stated.
No — the text says no AD is linked.

answer.text: not stated anywhere in the excerpt.

feedback.text: No — the compliance line states it clearly.

questiontext.text:
Read this airworthiness directive notice.

AD 2026-0142. Applies to all A320 aircraft, serials 5100–5200. Required action: inspect and replace the pitot bracket per SB 34-2189 rev 3. Compliance: mandatory within 12 months.

True or false: this notice makes the inspection mandatory.

generalfeedback.text: True. An airworthiness directive states a legal requirement; here compliance is "mandatory within 12 months".

feedback.text: Correct — an AD makes the action mandatory.
No — the AD states compliance is mandatory.

questiontext.text:
Read this work order line.

WORK ORDER 22-1043. Aircraft YL-BAP, serial 5133. Task: embody SB 34-2189 rev 3. Parts: order kit 34-2189-K3 (lead time 3 weeks). Note: no wiring rework.

What must the technician order?

generalfeedback.text: The Parts line says to order kit 34-2189-K3. The note confirms there is no wiring rework, so no wiring parts are needed.

feedback.text: No — the note says there is no wiring rework.
No — only the modification kit is listed.

questiontext.text:
Read this technical log entry.

SB 34-2189 rev 3 embodied on aircraft YL-BAK, serial 5127. Bracket replaced; area inspected; panel closed. No defects found. Embodiment recorded.

True or false: the entry records that the modification was completed and the embodiment logged.

generalfeedback.text: True. The entry states the SB was embodied, the work steps were done, and the embodiment was recorded — the proof of compliance.

feedback.text: Correct — the work is done and the embodiment recorded.
No — the entry clearly records the completed embodiment.

questiontext.text:
Make this an indirect question. Complete the clause in statement order (no do/does).

Direct: "Which effectivity applies?"

Could you tell me ____________ ?

generalfeedback.text: Keep the verb after the subject and drop any do/does: which effectivity applies. The verb "applies" carries the tense.

questiontext.text:
Make this an indirect question. It is a yes/no question, so use whether.

Direct: "Is the bulletin mandatory?"

Could you clarify ____________ ?

generalfeedback.text: A yes/no question needs whether (or if), then statement order: whether the bulletin is mandatory.

questiontext.text:
Fix the clause. Rewrite the embedded part in correct statement order.

Wrong: "Could you tell me what is the lead time?"

Could you tell me ____________ ?

generalfeedback.text: Do not keep the question inversion inside the clause. The verb "is" goes to the end: what the lead time is.

questiontext.text: Write the one term. The list of aircraft that a bulletin applies to is the ____________.

generalfeedback.text: applicability — the general list of aircraft a bulletin applies to. (The exact serial numbers are the effectivity.)

questiontext.text: Write the one term. A revision that has been replaced by a newer one is ____________.

generalfeedback.text: superseded — replaced by a newer version. Never use a superseded revision.

questiontext.text: Write the one term. After the modification, you record the ____________ with a logbook entry.

generalfeedback.text: embodiment — the state of a modification once it is fitted. You record it in the logbook, quoting the SB and revision.

questiontext.text: Match each term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: effectivity = exact serials · compliance = doing what is required · mandatory = you must · superseded = replaced · rework = extra work to redo.

answer.text: the exact serial numbers a bulletin covers
doing what a bulletin or directive requires
you must do it; it is not a choice
extra work to correct or redo something

questiontext.text: Match each term to the word it goes with.

generalfeedback.text: Collocations to learn: applicability table · airworthiness directive · logbook entry · lead time.

questiontext.text: Which term means "the original maker of the aircraft or part"?

generalfeedback.text: OEM = Original Equipment Manufacturer — the maker you call when the wording is unclear.

feedback.text: No — an AD is a legal order.
No — an SB is the maker's notice, not the maker.
No — the MEL is the minimum equipment list.

questiontext.text: Choose the natural collocation: "After the work, ____ the embodiment in the logbook."

generalfeedback.text: The verb that goes with "embodiment" is record: "record the embodiment". "Embody the modification" is also correct, but here the object is "the embodiment".

feedback.text: No — you supersede a revision, not an embodiment.
No — you clarify a question, not an embodiment.
No — dispatch does not collocate with embodiment.
